key_insight: Particle shape controls collective Marangoni surfing: prolate elliptical particles tend to attract, while oblate particles tend to repel.
engineering_relevance: The formulation offers a tractable route to modeling and coarse-graining shape-dependent interactions among surfactant-producing particles at fluid interfaces.
method: Assume low Reynolds and Péclet numbers.
Reduce surface–bulk coupling to integral equations on particles and their boundaries.
Use a custom spectral solver and far-field reduced-order model.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations reveal shape-sensitive collective dynamics and polarized-population stability, with behaviors rationalized by a far-field expansion.
watch_item: Applicability beyond the low-Reynolds, low-Péclet regime is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: A boundary integral formulation for microscale Marangoni surfing
